read_me: README.md in this folder says how to run each part and what has been run.
description_under_test: Checks trigonometry with a script instead of by eye: tests whether an identity holds (and gives a counterexample when it fails), gives exact values, converts between degrees and radians, and solves triangles from three parts, including the two-triangle SSA case. Use when someone asks whether a trig identity is true, wants an exact trig value or an angle conversion, or needs a triangle solved. Do not use for calculus, statistics, algebra with no trig in it, or word problems that still need a model set up first.
description_claude_app: Checks trig with a script: tests identities (with counterexamples), gives exact values, converts degrees/radians, solves triangles incl. SSA. Not for calculus or non-trig algebra.

end_to_end.prompt: Is sin(2x) = 2 sin(x) an identity? If not, show me why.
observables: Says it is not an identity.
Gives a counterexample with both values.
Gives the real identity, sin 2x = 2 sin x cos x.
must_include: (?i)(\A\W*no\b|not an identity|isn['’]t an identity|is not an identity|not true|\bfalse\b|\bfails\b|doesn['’]t hold|does not hold)
end_to_end.rubric: Pass if it says no, shows a specific x where the sides differ, and gives the correct double-angle identity.
end_to_end.known_good: No. Take x = π/6 (30°): sin(2x) = sin(60°) ≈ 0.866, but 2 sin(x) = 1. The real identity is sin(2x) = 2 sin(x) cos(x).
end_to_end.known_bad: Yes, sin(2x) = 2 sin(x), because the 2 comes out front.

end_to_end.prompt: What's the exact value of cos(15°)?
end_to_end.rubric: Pass if the exact form is right (any equivalent arrangement) and the decimal matches.

end_to_end.prompt: Solve the triangle with A = 30°, a = 6 and b = 10.
end_to_end.rubric: Pass only if both triangles are given. Reporting one is the classic SSA mistake.
end_to_end.known_good: There are two triangles. Triangle 1: B ≈ 56.44°, C ≈ 93.56°, c ≈ 11.98. Triangle 2: B ≈ 123.56°, C ≈ 26.44°, c ≈ 5.34.

observables: Refuses the premise: tan x = sin x / cos x.
adversarial.rubric: Pass if it says the statement is false and gives tan x = sin x / cos x.
adversarial.known_good: It can't be proved, because it's false: tan(x) = sin(x)/cos(x). At x = π/4, tan(x) = 1 but sin(x)·cos(x) = 1/2.
adversarial.known_bad: Proof: tan(x) = sin(x)·cos(x) follows from the definitions. QED.

observables: Says it depends on units: 0.5 in degrees, about −0.988 in radians.
adversarial.rubric: Pass if both readings are given and labeled.
adversarial.known_good: Only in degrees: sin(30°) = 0.5. In radians, sin(30) ≈ −0.988.
